title: The Toreador Hegemony
summary: How the Prince of Paris rules the Kindred of all France.

claims.text: The chief difference between the French and American Camarilla is the Hegemony, a rule the Prince of Paris forced on the provincial rulers from the late seventeenth century, often likened to absolute monarchy.
Under the Hegemony only François Villon bears the title of Prince; the rulers of other fiefs are Marquises, vassals of Paris.
Toreador rulers in the south kept the princely title until the Revolution swept them away; after the Restoration the Paris Toreador spread the Hegemony over every fief.
The Prince of Paris vetoes any Keeper of Elysium who is not Toreador, so the clan holds every Elysium in France.

title: Offices of a French Fief
summary: The posts that serve a Marquis.

claims.text: Besides the Marquis, the Legate and the Primogen, every French fief has a Seneschal, a Provost and a Keeper of Elysium; France is the only land where all three are found everywhere.
The Seneschal, also called Regent, is the Marquis's first adviser and stands in when the Marquis answers a summons from the Prince; the choice must be approved by Paris through the Legate.
The Provost works much like an American sheriff, seeing that the Marquis's rulings and the Traditions are obeyed and leading investigations and Blood Hunts.
The Paris fief covers the city and its suburbs, a great Toreador stronghold ruling over the arts, theater and fashion.
The Normandy fief spans Rouen, Caen and Le Havre and holds between nine and eighteen vampires in all.
The northern fief of Lille, Roubaix and Tourcoing was long run by the Ventrue and now answers to a Brujah Marquis, after more than a century of strife between factions.
Marseille is the oldest fief in France, founded by Brujah and Toreador who came from Greece.
